To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
contrastive learning can be used to recover the topic posterior information of documents and that this information is useful to linear classifiers in document classification tasks.

(1) contrastive learning reveals the topic posterior information to classifiers, (2) the resulting linear classifiers can perform as well as state-of-the-art non-linear classifiers in semi-supervised document classification tasks with few training examples, (3) the linear classifiers are interpretable and (4) the resulting representations can be used to improve topic modeling performance.

The main takeaway from our work is that
contrastive learning provides a useful tool for learning representations that reveal the underlying structure of data to simple models.

, under topic modeling assumptions and with the right contrastive learning procedure, linear models can be made to perform surprisingly well on tasks that are traditionally considered hard for linear methods.
